title: Almighty God, in Humble Prayer
description: Almighty God, in Humble Prayer in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 43, “Prayer for Wisdom”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Al-might-y God, in hum-ble prayer To Thee our souls we lift; Do Thou our wait-ing minds pre-pare For Thy most need-ful gift.

lines: To Thee our souls we lift;
Do Thou our waiting minds prepare
We ask not golden streams of wealth
We ask not honors, which an hour
We ask not pleasure, pomp, or power,
We ask for wisdom: Lord, impart
The young remember Thee in youth,
The old be guided by Thy truth

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
